Package org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr

Class Cons

java.lang.Object
org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr.Datum
org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr.Cons
Direct Known Subclasses:
ConsCell, ConsList, ConsTail
public abstract non-sealed class Cons extends Datum
An immutable pair of Datums. A chain of cons cells created by recursively storing cons cells in the cdr forms a list.

If the list terminates with a meaningless datum (i.e., nil), it is considered proper. It is otherwise considered improper.

This is a non-sealed class so that it is possible to specialize storage backend. In return, we ask that any subclass provides the same immutable, acyclic structure as the naive implementation with ConsCell. Acyclicity is generally trivially satisfied when car and cdr are stored as final datum fields, but it is something to be look out for when car and cdr are instead dynamically generated.

    • equals

      public final boolean equals(Object o)
      Returns whether this equals o. Two cons cells are equal if their cars are equal and their cdrs are equal.
      Specified by:
      equals in class Datum
      Parameters:
      o - object to compare
      Returns:
      whether this equals o
      Since:
      0.1.0
      Implementation Note:
      This implementation uses a stack to compare cons children, instead of recursion which can overflow the stack memory fast. Cached hash codes are used to reject peers early, but they are not expected, and will not be populated if absent.

    • hashCode

      public final int hashCode()
      Returns hash code for this. Equal cons cells hash to the same code.
      Specified by:
      hashCode in class Datum
      Returns:
      hash code for this
      Since:
      0.1.0
      Implementation Note:
      This implementation uses a stack to traverse cons children with an absent hash, instead of recursion which can overflow the stack memory fast. The hash is cached; and because 0 is used as the sentinel, it never returns 0. (The choice of 0 is arbitrary.)

    • of

      public static Cons of(Deque<? extends Datum> q, Cons p)
      Prefixes a cons chain with a deque. Elements are popped from the front and prepended one at a time, reversing their iteration order. This drains the deque and is thus destructive!
      Parameters:
      q - the deque
      p - base cons chain
      Returns:
      the concatenated cons chain
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if any argument or deque element is null
      Since:
      0.1.0
